NOISE IMPACT
Introduction
This section presents the assessment of potential noise impacts associated with the
construction and operation of the Project. The noise impact assessment has been
conducted in accordance with the requirement of Annex 5 and Annex 13 of the
Technical Memorandum on Environmental Impact Assessment Process (EIAO-TM)
as well as the requirements set out in Clause 3.5.4 of the Environmental Impact
Assessment (EIA) Study Brief (No. ESB-375/2025).
Environmental Legislation, Standards and Guidelines
Noise impact has been assessed in accordance with the criteria and methodology
given in the Technical Memoranda (TM) under the Noise Control Ordinance (NCO),
and the EIAO-TM, Guidance Notes under EIAO (EIAO-GN).
Assessment procedures and standards are set out in the following TMs and Guidance
Notes:-
• Technical Memorandum on Environmental Impact Assessment Process (EIAO-
TM);

Domestic Premises, Public Places or Construction Sites (IND-TM);

Percussive Piling (GW-TM);

• EIAO-GN 9/2023 Preparation of Construction Noise Impact Assessment under
the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (EIAO);

Under the EIAO; and
• EIAO-GN 12/2023 Road Traffic Noise Impact Assessment under the EIAO.
Construction Noise Criteria
General Construction Works
The NCO provides the statutory framework for noise control of construction works,
other than percussive piling, using powered mechanical equipment (PME) between
the hours of 1900 and 0700 hours or at any time on Sundays and general holiday
(i.e. restricted hours). Noise from construction activities taking place at 0700 to 1900
hours on any day not being a Sunday or general holiday is subject to the Noise
Standards for Daytime Construction Activities stated in Table 1B of Annex 5 in the
EIAO-TM. The criteria are summarised in Table 4.1.

According to the latest land use plan under “Agreement No. CE 46/2022 – Ma Tso
Lung Area and Other Sites in Kwu Tung North New Development Area and North
District – Feasibility Study (hereinafter referred to as “MTL Project”)”, Site Res 3 and

detailed building layout plans for the potential residential development at Site Res 3
and Site Res 6 were not yet available. Therefore, an assessment point has been
conservatively selected at the boundary of these sites for evaluation purposes.
Based on the latest available information, the construction of MTL Project is
anticipated to commence in Year 2028 with population intake expected in Year 2034,
which is after the completion of the Project (i.e. Year 2031). As such, the assessment
points at Site Res 3 and Site Res 6 have been included for operation phase
assessment only. The maximum proposed building height for Sites Res 3 and Res 6
is +155mPD. For the purpose of the assessment, it was assumed that the planned
NSRs at Sites Res 3 and Res 6 will have up to 45 storeys. It is noted that the
construction of Project will commence in Year 2027, while the MTL Project
construction is tentatively scheduled for 2028 to 2034. As such, some existing NSRs
which fall under the MTL Project area, may be affected by construction noise impacts
from the Project. Accordingly, these existing NSRs have been identified for the
construction phase assessment.
With reference to the latest Outline Zoning Plan (OZP) (Approved Lok Ma Chau Loop
Outline Zone Plan No. S/LMCL/2 1 ), certain Other Specified Uses (OU) and
Government, Institution or Community (G/IC) zonings are reserved for non-noise
sensitive uses, including district cooling system, sewage treatment works and
electricity substation. The northwest G/IC zoning is reserved for fire station-cum-
ambulance depot, Hong Kong Police Force (HKPF) facilities and boundary crossing
facilities. It is assumed that these facilities, along with the planned commercial uses
will not rely on opened windows for ventilation and are therefore considered as noise
tolerant. According to the Outline Zoning Plan (OZP), the "Other Specified Uses" (OU)
zoning located on the southwestern side of the Project is designated for research and
development, education, and cultural and creative industries. This zone is planned to
accommodate student hostels, staff quarters, academic buildings, and administrative
facilities. As stated in the approved EIA Report for the Development of Lok Ma Chau
Loop (AEIAR-176/2013), central air conditioning is assumed to be provided for
academic and administrative buildings. Therefore, only the student hostels and staff
quarters are considered NSRs.

(NAPs) for construction noise, road traffic noise and fixed noise impact assessments
are presented in 60722948/A10/FIGURE 4.2, 4.3, and 4.6. A list of the representative
NSRs and NAPs are presented in Table 4.6 to Table 4.8. The photographs of the
existing NSRs are presented in Appendix 4.1.
In order to evaluate the noise impacts during construction and operation phases
associated with the Project, representative existing/planned NSRs located within the
assessment area have been identified for assessment. Only the first layer of NSRs
have been identified for assessment because it would provide acoustic shielding to
those receivers at further distance behind.

In accordance with the requirements given in the Clause 1.2.2 of Appendix C of Study

• Identify the major noise sources and construction activities;
• Evaluate the potential impact on the NSRs qualitatively;
• Propose suitable mitigation measures such as quieter construction method and
equipment, barrier, enclosure, etc; and
• Propose to submit a Construction Noise Management Plan (CNMP), which
contains quantitative construction noise impact assessment, to EPD.

presented in Section 4.7.1.

effects due to gradient, distance, view angle, road surface and barriers would be
included in the assessment.

In order to reduce the excessive construction noise impact at the NSRs, applicable
quieter construction method and PME are identified below. Further mitigation
measures of movable noise barriers and temporary noise barriers are also
recommended.
Quieter construction method such as silent piling by press-in method is adopted as
an alternative of traditional sheet piling. A sheet pile is clipped and pressed under the
ground. Noise can be minimised by press-in sheet piles with drilling simultaneously
for piling works at harder ground. The noise impact can also be further reduced as
the piling works can be completed within the shorter duration by using this method.
Another quieter construction method for piling works is the large diameter bored piling
method, which would replace percussive piling for piling works.
Other quieter construction method includes the precast concrete construction method
(refer to Section 2 for details on construction method). The precasting works will be
carried out in the fabrication yard away from the site, which reduces the amount of
mechanical equipment used on site such as concrete mixing trucks and therefore
reducing the potential noise impact. This method can also further reduce the noise
impact by allowing non-linear bridge deck construction across multiple work fronts
within the shorter duration.
It is also feasible to adopt quieter rock or concrete breaking equipment (e.g. hydraulic
rock crusher) in some activities as a mitigation measure. The Contractor should,
subject to the actual site conditions, proactively adopt quieter rock breaking
equipment and hydraulic crusher to replace hydraulic breaker for rock or concrete
breaking to carry out the demolition / excavation works, where practicable. This
method can further reduce the noise impact by percussive striking actions of
breaker’s chisels.
The Contractor(s) may be able to obtain particular models of plant that are quieter
than the PMEs given in GW-TM. The use of quality PME associated with the
construction works is prescribed in EPD’s Quality Powered Mechanical Equipment
(QPME) database, which contains the SWLs for quality/quiet PME of various types,
brands and models. The Contractor should, subject to the actual site conditions,
proactively adopt quality PME in all kinds of construction activities, where practicable.
The Contractor should select appropriate quieter construction method / equipment to
minimise any potential construction noise impact to the environment. A list of quieter

The Contractor should review the applicability of quiet construction method, quieter
electric construction equipment, QPME, quieter rock breaking equipment and the use
of hydraulic crusher instead of rock breaking. Other available noise-reducing
technologies and practices should also be considered to further minimise potential
construction noise impacts. These quieter construction method and equipment shall
be clearly specified in a Construction Noise Mitigation Plan (CNMP) and incorporated
into the tender documents during tendering process.
To alleviate the construction noise impact on the affected NSRs, movable noise
barriers have been proposed. Movable temporary noise barriers that can be located
close to noisy plant and be moved iteratively with the plant along a worksite can be
very effective for screening noise from NSRs. A typical design which has been used
locally is a wooden framed barrier with a small cantilevered upper portion of
superficial density no less than 14kg/m2 on a skid footing with 25mm thick internal
sound absorptive lining. The measure is particularly effective for low level zone of
NSRs. A cantilevered top cover would be required to achieve screening benefits at
high level of NSRs. It is anticipated that suitably designed barriers could achieve at
least 5-10 dB(A) reduction.
The use of full enclosure has been proposed in this assessment to shelter relatively
static plant including air compressor and generator. This type of enclosure is
expected to provide approximately 15 dB(A) noise reduction.
The benefits of these techniques may vary with specific site conditions and operations.
The environmental noise climate would certainly be improved with these control
practices, although the improvement can only be quantified during implementation
when specific site parameters are known.
The CNMP as detailed in EIAO-GN 9/2023 would be submitted to the Director of the
EPD for agreement prior to issuance of tender and commencement of construction.
The CNMP shall contain quantitative construction noise impact assessment, adopted
quieter construction method and equipment, noise mitigation measures, and
construction noise monitoring and auditing programme, with reference to the latest
plant inventories and an implementation schedule clearly listing out the mitigation
measures, the implementation party, location, and timing of implementation for
inclusion in the tender document, if any. Mitigation measures recommended and
requirements specified in the CNMP shall be fully implemented. Any technical
constraint that would hinder the use of these quieter construction method and
equipment shall be evaluated and clearly recorded in the CNMP.

Operation Phase (Fixed Noise)
In view of the potential fixed noise impact arising from the proposed pumping station,
direct mitigation measures should be considered at source to minimise the potential
fixed noise impact. Direct mitigation measures include using quieter fixed plant, use
of silencer, installation of acoustic louvre, installation of noise barrier, and installation
of noise enclosure, etc. would be recommended to minimise the potential fixed noise
sources impact from the proposed fixed noise sources, such that the fixed noise level
would comply with the criteria at the NSR.
A Fixed Noise Sources Management Plan (FNMP) as detailed in EIAO-GN 16/2023
would be submitted to Director of the EPD for agreement prior to issuance of tender
and commencement of construction of the proposed fixed noise sources. The FNMP
shall contain quantitative fixed noise source impact assessment with the latest list of
fixed noise source plant inventory, recommended noise mitigation measures,
commissioning test requirements and environmental monitoring and audit
programme. FNMP shall include an implementation schedule clearly listing out the
mitigation measures, the implementation party, location, and timing of
implementation. Mitigation measures recommended and requirements specified in
the FNMP shall be fully implemented.
